# Recall



* Pros and cons of the three modes of communication: speech\, sign\, writing
* __Writing__  is the representation of language with the use of visual signs
  * So\, not pictograms
  * Iconic vs\. symbolic
  * Phonological or morphological
* Writing is  __learned__
  * But certain aspects of  __computer\-mediated communication __ \(CMC\) seem like they are acquired
  * Emojis as extralinguistic material \(like facial expressions and body language\)
* What makes the digital environment different from face\-to\-face?

# Computational linguistics

![](images/19-Why%20can%E2%80%99t%20Siri%20pronounce%20my%20name_0.jpg)



* __Computational linguistics __ is the area of linguistics that computer scientists like…
  * Linguistics \+ computers = you can rule the world\!
  * If you are looking for the most lucrative field\, this is it\!
* Computational linguistics is about:
  * Speech synthesis
  * Automatic \(computer\) recognition of speech
  * Machine translation
  * Corpus construction

# Talking to machines?



* One thing that has become ever\-present in our lives is the digital world
  * You can speak your text message to your phone – this is called  __speech\-to\-text__
  * You can have your text messages read aloud by your phone – this is called  __text\-to\-speech__
* Speech technologies are increasingly integrated into our lives\!
  * Everyone is obsessed with AI
  * There are refrigerators\, cars\, etc\. with built\-in speech technologies
  * Your phone might have a virtual assistant\, like Siri


![](images/19-Why%20can%E2%80%99t%20Siri%20pronounce%20my%20name_1.png)

![](images/19-Why%20can%E2%80%99t%20Siri%20pronounce%20my%20name_2.jpg)

# Speech recognition and synthesis



* Your devices rely on  __speech recognition technologies__ \, which means that they have the ability to recognize and translate human spoken language into text that can be understood by computers
  * This allows you to use commands like “call Mom”
  * Has a wide array of applications
* They also rely on  __speech synthesis__ \, which is the artificial production of human speech by a computer
  * They sound so real now
  * Here’s how it used to sound…

# Performance



* Speech recognition is complex
  * Background noise can get in the way
  * Linguistic variation can be tricky to capture
* I said they were getting better – how do we know?
  * __Accuracy__  – how often does the system get it wrong?
  * __Speed__  – how quickly does it convert from speech to text?

# Linguistic variation



* Has Siri had trouble understanding what you’ve said?
* Some of the accuracy issues may have been part of the problem\, but often\, linguistic variation in accent\, word choice\, etc\. can be the problem
* Research has shown that
  * African Americans experience error rates up to two times higher than other speakers of American English
    * Word identification is less accurate\, but
    * Word prediction is sometimes better compared to majority dialects
  * Linguists use “force\-aligners” to automatically transcribe speech\, and one study found that error rates on accuracy were higher for Southern varieties compared to Northern ones

---


![](images/19-Why%20can%E2%80%99t%20Siri%20pronounce%20my%20name_6.png)



* Proportion of correctly recognized words by dialect area\, color coded by country
  * Used YouTube auto\-captions on Accent Tag videos \(powered by Google\)
  * Works best on people from California \(which just happens to be where Google is headquartered\)
  * Works worst on Scottish English
